info.name: Hybrid Ops Agent — UserAdmin + SupportDesk
info.description:
Hybrid orchestration API for the UserAdmin (Product 1) and SupportDesk (Product 2) agents.

`POST /orchestrate` is the single entry point: a classifier agent routes each request to one of four deterministic flows (suspend-by-domain, bulk-create-from-CSV, resolve-billing-ticket, triage-ticket) or to the model-driven (Mode A) agent, which now carries both domains' tools. The `Flows (direct)` folder bypasses the classifier for callers that already know which flow they want. The remaining routes are read-only inspection endpoints.

Set the `base_url` and `actor` collection variables (Variables tab) before running. The `demo_*` variables point at the three fixed demo tickets/subscription seeded every boot specifically for exercising Product 2's guardrails (see README.md → "Things to try") — they're stable across reseeds since they're generated deterministically, not via Math.random().

Note: `/orchestrate`, `/orchestrate/classify`, and both Product 2 `/flows/*` endpoints call Claude, so `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` must be set on the server. The two Product 1 `/flows/*` endpoints and everything under `Inspection (read-only)` do not.

variable.description: Seeded ticket: "Can you refund me $120…" — no legal keywords, amount between autoApproveMaxCents and requiresApprovalMaxCents. Isolates the dollar-policy layer.
Seeded ticket: "Refund my $500 or I'll escalate this to legal." — the spec's literal adversarial sentence. Fires the keyword guardrail regardless of REFUND_POLICY_ENFORCEMENT.
Seeded ticket with a 30-message alternating thread, for exercising COMPACTION_ENABLED.
The dollar-policy demo user's subscription (enterprise, mrr_cents=19900, renewed today).

item.name: Orchestrator
item.description: The single entry point. Classify + execute, or classify only.

request.description: A single-user request the classifier routes to `model_driven`. The Mode A run is nested under `agent_result`; `flow_result` is null.

item.name: Orchestrate — deterministic flow 1: suspend by domain (escalates)

request.description: The seeded users are all @example.com, so thousands match (> 3, includes admins) → the flow escalates instead of suspending. Result lands in `flow_result` with `decision: "escalated"`.

item.name: Orchestrate — deterministic flow 1: suspend by domain (auto-suspend)

request.description: A small/non-privileged domain (≤ 3 matches, no admins, not high risk) auto-suspends. Against the default seed data acme.com has no matches (`decision: "no_matches"`); create a few acme.com users first (flow 2) to see a real suspension.

item.name: Orchestrate — deterministic flow 2: bulk create from CSV

request.description: Parses the CSV and creates each row. Valid rows land in `flow_result.created`; the malformed email is reported in `flow_result.failed` (partial success).
Routes to model-driven; the agent should call escalate_to_human, so `agent_result.escalation` is populated.

item.name: Orchestrate — deterministic flow 3: resolve billing ticket (rejected under code_enforced)

request.description: Routes to `resolve_billing_ticket`. With the default REFUND_POLICY_ENFORCEMENT=code_enforced, the $120 request is rejected (above autoApproveMaxCents with no approval_flag) and escalated. Restart the server with REFUND_POLICY_ENFORCEMENT=prompt_only and re-run to see it auto-refund instead — the single most exam-relevant comparison in this collection.

item.name: Orchestrate — universal ticket guardrail fires even though classifier picks model_driven

request.description: The prompt is vague enough that `classification.route` comes back `model_driven` — but the response's top-level `route` reads `deterministic` anyway, because OrchestratorService's universal pre-dispatch guardrail catches the flagged ticket_id and escalates before Mode A ever runs. Demonstrates `route` ≠ `classification.route`.

No ticket referenced, so no deterministic flow matches — routes to Mode A, which calls the new `search_kb` tool from the merged SupportDesk tool set. Good place to watch `cache_creation_input_tokens` on turn 1 and `cache_read_input_tokens` on later turns in `agent_result.turns[].usage`.
Returns the classifier's routing decision (route, flow, extracted domain/csv_text/ticket_id, tool_sequence, reasoning) without running anything.

item.name: Classify only — ticket vs. domain disambiguation

request.description: Contains the word "suspend" but references a specific ticket — the classifier's system prompt disambiguates this to `resolve_billing_ticket`, not `suspend_users_by_domain`. Compare against the plain domain-suspension classify call above.

item.name: Flows (direct)
item.description: Bypass the classifier entirely for callers that already know which workflow they want. Same "empty/invalid input → HTTP 200 with { error }" convention as /orchestrate. The two Product 2 flows call Claude (the classify step) and need ANTHROPIC_API_KEY; the two Product 1 flows never call Claude.

request.description: Runs SuspendByDomainFlow directly. Never calls Claude.

Takes a rows array directly (no CSV parsing), unlike bulk_create_users_from_csv. All-or-nothing validation phase first, then one atomic write. Never calls Claude. This example includes a duplicate-in-batch row and an invalid-format row to show the per-row `results[]` skip reasons.

Runs ResolveBillingTicketFlow directly against the seeded dollar-policy demo ticket. Calls Claude (the classify step) — needs ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. Under the default REFUND_POLICY_ENFORCEMENT=code_enforced, expect decision:"escalated"; under prompt_only, expect decision:"refunded".

item.name: Resolve billing ticket (direct) — legal/security guardrail demo

request.description: The keyword-filter demo ticket ("…I'll escalate this to legal"). The legal/security pre-filter fires before the classify step ever runs — escalates immediately regardless of REFUND_POLICY_ENFORCEMENT, with the full thread packaged into escalation.full_thread.

item.name: Triage ticket (direct) — billing category, hands off to resolve flow

request.description: Runs TriageTicketFlow. The compaction-demo ticket is a billing dispute, so the cheap category classifier picks "billing" and hands off to ResolveBillingTicketFlow (nested under billing_result).

item.name: Triage ticket (direct) — legal category via keyword pre-filter

request.description: The keyword pre-filter catches this before the cheap category classifier even runs — category comes back "legal" with reasoning "Pre-filter matched: legal", and the ticket is marked escalated. No Claude call needed to reach this result.

item.name: Inspection (read-only)
item.description: Handy while poking at the seeded data. None of these call Claude, so they work with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset.

query.description: Free text matched against email or name (empty = all).

request.description: Free-text search over email and name, optionally filtered by role/status/country/city. Returns up to 50 summaries.
Full record for a single user.
Recent audit-log rows (every mutating action writes one, including issue_refund with its enforcement_mode), newest first.
Full ticket record (subject, body, status, user_id, created_at).
The full message thread, oldest first. The compaction-demo ticket has 30 alternating customer/agent messages.
